set1.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set1.q: Why is phase 2 called the plateau?
opts: All ion movement stops entirely
Ions continue to move; it is the balance between two currents that holds the voltage steady.
Calcium entering the cell is matched by potassium moving the other way
Correct, and the calcium entering during this balance is what actually produces contraction, so the flat part of the trace is the working part of the beat. So the voltage holds.
Sodium continues to enter at a constant rate
Sodium channels have closed by this point; the inward current here is calcium.
The cell has returned to its resting voltage and remains there
The plateau sits well above the resting voltage, which is reached again at the end of phase three.

set1.io: Determine heart rate using an electrocardiogram
set1.q: Which relationship is checked when assessing P waves on a strip?
opts: Whether the P wave is taller than the T wave
Relative amplitude is not the check; it is whether each P has a QRS and each QRS a P.
Whether the P wave falls within the QT interval
The QT interval covers ventricular activity and does not contain the P wave.
Whether there is a P wave for every QRS complex and a QRS for every P wave
Correct. It is a two-way check, and each direction fails in a different way, which is what makes the blocks distinguishable.
Whether the P wave is visible in all twelve leads
The described check concerns the relationship with the QRS rather than visibility across leads.

set1.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set1.q: Which structure is described as the third pacemaker, taking over if both the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes fail?
opts: The bundle of His
The bundle of His is the connection between the atrioventricular node and the bundle branches rather than the third pacemaker.
The Purkinje network
Correct, at an intrinsic rate of twenty to forty -- slow enough to be a last resort rather than a comfortable substitute.
The left anterior fascicle
The fascicles are branches of the conducting pathway rather than a named pacemaker.
The internodal tracts
These connect the sinoatrial node to the atrioventricular node rather than pacing the heart.

set1.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set1.q: The overall vector at a given moment is directed away from a lead. What does that lead record?
opts: A positive deflection
A positive deflection means the vector is directed toward the lead.
An isoelectric line
An isoelectric line means the net vector is zero rather than directed away.
No tracing at all
The lead still records; a vector directed away simply produces a downward deflection.
A negative deflection
Correct, and the converse holds: toward the lead gives a positive deflection, which is why the same beat looks different in different leads.

set1.io: Determine heart rate using an electrocardiogram
set1.q: How is the ATRIAL rate obtained by the six-second method?
opts: Count the QRS complexes and multiply by ten
That gives the ventricular rate; the atrial rate needs the P waves.
Count the T waves and multiply by ten
The T wave is a ventricular event and is not counted for atrial rate.
Measure the PR interval and divide into sixty
The PR interval is not used to derive a rate; P waves are counted over six seconds instead.
Count the P waves in six seconds and multiply by ten
Correct, and doing both counts separately is what reveals a heart block, where the two rates differ.

set1.io: Define absolute and relative refractory periods
set1.q: Over which part of the action potential does the ABSOLUTE refractory period run?
opts: From the middle of phase 3 to the end of phase 3
That span is the RELATIVE refractory period, in which a strong enough stimulus can succeed.
Throughout phase 4
Phase four is the resting state, in which the cell is ready to respond rather than refractory.
From phase 1 to phase 2 only
The absolute period begins at the upstroke and extends well past the plateau.
From phase 0 to the middle of phase 3
Correct, and it lasts about a hundred and eighty milliseconds, during which no stimulus of any strength will produce another action potential.

set1.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set1.q: What distinguishes a SEGMENT from an INTERVAL?
opts: A segment includes a wave; an interval is the flat line between waves
The definitions are the other way round: the segment is the flat line and the interval contains waves.
They are two names for the same thing
They are distinguished explicitly: one contains waves and the other does not.
A segment is the flat line between two waves
Correct. An interval is the larger unit, which is why the PR interval contains the PR segment rather than being the same thing. An interval includes at least one wave plus at least one segment.
A segment is measured in millivolts and an interval in seconds
Both are spans of time along the tracing; the difference is whether a wave is included.

set1.io: Identify the standard limb and precordial leads and their proper anatomical placement
set1.q: Which six electrocardiographic leads do the four limb electrodes produce?
opts: Leads I, II and III together with aVR, aVL and aVF
Correct. These six are the hexaxial leads, and they are what the hexaxial reference system uses to determine the axis.
V1 through V6
The precordial leads come from six separate chest electrodes.
Leads I, II and III only
The augmented leads are derived from the same limb electrodes, making six in all.
aVR, aVL and aVF only
Leads I, II and III come from the same electrodes and complete the six.

set1.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set1.q: What two things does the atrioventricular node do to the impulse passing through it?
opts: It introduces a short pause and amplifies the signal
Correct. The pause is what lets the atria finish emptying before the ventricles contract, so a delay in the conduction system is doing useful mechanical work.
It speeds the impulse up and attenuates it
It delays rather than accelerates, and it amplifies rather than attenuates.
It blocks every second impulse by design
Blocking alternate impulses is a pathological pattern rather than normal nodal behaviour.
It reverses the direction of the impulse
The impulse continues onward toward the ventricles; the node delays and amplifies it rather than reversing it.

set1.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set1.q: In which direction does conduction truly travel through the heart?
opts: Right and up, toward the shoulder
The described pathway runs leftward and downward rather than to the right and upward.
Left and down, toward the anterior chest
Correct, and this is why lead II sees the beat so well: it looks along that axis.
Straight downward, in the coronal plane only
The described direction has a leftward and anterior component as well as a downward one.
Posteriorly, away from the chest wall
It runs left and down toward the anterior chest rather than posteriorly away from it.

set1.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set1.q: What does the Q wave represent, and why is it negative in lead II?
opts: Depolarisation of the anterior left ventricle, travelling toward lead II
That is the R wave, and travelling toward the lead is why it is positive.
Depolarisation of the lateral wall of the left ventricle
That is the S wave, which like the Q wave travels away from lead II and so deflects downward.
Depolarisation of the interventricular septum, which travels away from lead II
Correct. The direction of that particular wavefront is what makes the deflection downward, and it is not always visible.
Repolarisation of the ventricles
Ventricular repolarisation is the T wave rather than any part of the QRS complex.

set1.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set1.q: What happens during phase 0, the upstroke?
opts: Fast sodium channels open and sodium rushes into the cell
Correct. It is the fastest event in the cycle, and the rapid inward sodium current is what drives the voltage positive.
Calcium channels open and calcium enters the cell
Calcium entry belongs to phase two, the plateau, and it is what triggers contraction.
Potassium channels open and potassium leaves the cell
Potassium movement dominates the repolarising phases rather than the upstroke.
Sodium is actively pumped out of the cell
Active extrusion restores the gradient over time; the upstroke is a passive rapid influx.

set1.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set1.q: What happens during phase 3, rapid repolarisation?
opts: Calcium channels close while potassium channels remain open, returning the cell to minus ninety millivolts
Correct. The inward current stops and the outward one continues unopposed, which is why this phase is the rapid one.
Calcium channels open and the voltage rises
Calcium entry belongs to the plateau; in phase three the calcium channels close.
Fast sodium channels reopen
Sodium channel reopening does not occur here; the cell is returning toward rest.
The membrane holds at a steady plateau voltage
The steady plateau is phase two; phase three is the fall away from it.

set1.io: Identify the standard limb and precordial leads and their proper anatomical placement
set1.q: Which of these is one of the described contiguous groups?
opts: Leads II, III and aVF
Correct. The other two groups are V1 to V4, and leads I, aVL, V5 and V6.
Leads I, II and III
These three are the bipolar limb leads rather than a contiguous group.
Leads aVR, aVL and aVF
These are the augmented leads rather than a contiguous group.
Leads V1, V3 and V5
The described group runs V1 to V4 consecutively rather than alternating.

set1.io: Define absolute and relative refractory periods
set1.q: What distinguishes the relative from the absolute refractory period?
opts: In the relative period a sufficiently strong stimulus can produce a response
Correct. It is the dangerous window: the cell is excitable again but not yet fully recovered, so a stimulus arriving there can start something abnormal.
In the relative period no stimulus of any strength will produce a response
That describes the absolute period; the relative one can be overcome.
The relative period occurs before the absolute period
It runs from the middle to the end of phase three, after the absolute period.
The relative period occupies the whole of phase 4
Phase four is the resting state, in which the cell responds normally.

set1.io: Determine heart rate using an electrocardiogram
set1.q: What is the R to R interval used to assess?
opts: Rate, regularity
Correct. One measurement doing three jobs, which is why comparing consecutive R to R intervals is the first thing done to a strip. Heart blocks.
Ventricular repolarisation
Ventricular repolarisation is assessed from the T wave and the QT interval.
Atrial depolarisation
Atrial depolarisation is assessed from the P wave rather than from the R to R interval.
The isoelectric baseline
The baseline is assessed on the TP segment rather than from the R to R interval.

set1.io: Determine heart rate using an electrocardiogram
set1.q: How is regularity determined when it is not obvious by eye?
opts: By counting the number of P waves in six seconds
Counting in six seconds gives a rate rather than a judgement of regularity.
By comparing consecutive R to R intervals with calipers
Correct. The marked paper is the field substitute, and it answers the same question the calipers do. Or a marked sheet of paper.
By measuring the QT interval in several leads
The QT interval does not address regularity; consecutive R to R intervals are what is compared.
By assessing the isoelectric line on the TP segment
The TP segment establishes the baseline rather than the regularity.

set1.io: Determine heart rate using an electrocardiogram
set1.q: What limits the use of the three hundred method?
opts: It only works on a six-second strip
The six-second requirement belongs to the other method; this one requires a regular rhythm.
It only works in lead II
Lead choice is not the limitation; the method requires the rhythm to be regular.
It only works at rates above one hundred
The limitation concerns regularity rather than the rate itself.
It only works if the rhythm is regular
Correct, which is why regularity is assessed before rate: the answer decides which method may be used.

set1.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set1.q: What is distinctive about the bundle of His in a normal heart?
opts: It is one of several pathways crossing the atrioventricular junction
In a normal heart it is the only one; additional pathways are abnormal.
It paces the heart at sixty to a hundred beats per minute
That intrinsic rate belongs to the sinoatrial node; the bundle of His is a conducting pathway rather than a pacemaker.
It is the only electrical pathway crossing from the atria to the ventricles
Correct. Everything above and below has to go through it, which is why a block there separates the two halves of the heart electrically.
It lies within the atrial wall
It connects the atrioventricular node to the bundle branches across the nonconductive wall between the chambers.

set1.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set1.q: Reading left to right across the paper measures time. What does reading up and down measure?
opts: Rate
Rate is derived from how many complexes occupy a span of time along the horizontal axis.
Voltage
Correct, and at standard calibration a small box is a tenth of a millivolt, with a ten millimetre deflection equal to one millivolt.
Time in a second dimension
Time runs along the horizontal axis only; the vertical axis measures voltage.
Conduction velocity
Velocity is not read from the vertical axis, which measures voltage in millivolts.

set1.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set1.q: What is happening mechanically during the ST segment?
opts: The ventricles are filling during diastole
Filling corresponds to the resting portion of the cycle rather than the ST segment.
The atria are contracting
Atrial activity occurs earlier, around the P wave; the ST segment is a ventricular event.
The ventricles are holding their contraction to allow emptying
Correct. It falls between ventricular depolarisation and repolarisation, and it is the part of the beat that does the ejecting.
The ventricles are repolarising
Ventricular repolarisation is the T wave, which follows the ST segment.

set1.io: Identify the standard limb and precordial leads and their proper anatomical placement
set1.q: What view of the heart do the precordial leads give?
opts: A frontal view
The frontal plane is covered by the limb and augmented leads.
A horizontal view
Correct, which complements the frontal plane the limb leads provide, so the two sets together look at the heart from two directions.
A sagittal view only
The described view is horizontal, complementing the frontal plane the limb leads provide.
No spatial view; they measure rate only
They provide a horizontal spatial view rather than a rate measurement.

set1.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set1.q: Prominent U waves are associated with which conditions?
opts: Hyperkalaemia and hypocalcaemia
The associations described run the other way for both electrolytes.
Atrial fibrillation
Atrial fibrillation is not among the described associations.
Hypokalaemia, hypercalcaemia, prolonged QT and the period after myocardial infarction
Correct, and the electrolyte associations are the practically useful ones, since the wave itself is not fully understood.
Pericardial effusion
Pericardial disease is not among the described associations.

set1.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set1.q: A heart is being paced at a rate in the forties, with no sinoatrial activity. Which pacemaker is most likely responsible?
opts: The sinoatrial node
The sinoatrial node paces at sixty to a hundred, and the question states it is not firing.
The atrioventricular node
Correct. Its intrinsic rate is forty to sixty, and it takes over as the backup when the sinoatrial node fails.
The Purkinje network
The Purkinje network paces more slowly still, at twenty to forty.
The bundle of His alone
The bundle of His conducts rather than being described as an independent pacemaker with its own rate.

set1.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set1.q: Which ion entering the cell during the plateau causes contraction?
opts: Sodium
Sodium drives the upstroke in phase zero rather than the contraction, which calcium triggers.
Calcium
Correct. It is the link between the electrical event and the mechanical one, which is why the plateau is where excitation becomes contraction.
Potassium
Potassium movement repolarises the cell rather than triggering contraction.
Chloride
Chloride is not among the ions described in these phases; sodium, potassium and calcium are.

set1.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set1.q: What does the R wave represent?
opts: Depolarisation of the interventricular septum
That is the Q wave, the first negative deflection following the PR interval.
Depolarisation of the lateral wall of the left ventricle
That is the S wave, the first negative deflection following the R wave.
Depolarisation of the atria
Atrial depolarisation is the P wave rather than any component of the QRS complex.
Depolarisation of the anterior left ventricle
Correct, and it is the first positive deflection, following either the PR interval or the Q wave.

set1.io: Determine heart rate using an electrocardiogram
set1.q: A six-second strip contains eight QRS complexes. What is the ventricular rate?
opts: Eighty beats per minute
Correct. The six-second method multiplies the count by ten, since six seconds is a tenth of a minute.
Forty-eight beats per minute
That would follow from multiplying by six rather than by ten.
Eight beats per minute
That is the raw count over six seconds rather than the rate per minute.
One hundred and sixty beats per minute
That would follow from doubling the correct figure; the six-second count is multiplied by ten.

set1.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set1.q: What does the QRS complex represent, and what should it look like?
opts: Ventricular repolarisation, broad and rounded
Ventricular repolarisation is the T wave, which is broad and rounded.
Atrial depolarisation, narrow and upright
Atrial depolarisation is the P wave rather than the QRS complex, which is ventricular.
The plateau phase of the action potential
The plateau corresponds to the ST segment rather than to the QRS.
Ventricular depolarisation, narrow with sharp points
Correct, with a duration under three small boxes. A wide QRS means the ventricles were not activated through the normal fast pathway.

set1.io: Identify the standard limb and precordial leads and their proper anatomical placement
set1.q: What is the hexaxial reference system used to determine?
opts: The heart rate
Rate is determined from the strip by the six-second or three hundred method rather than from the axis system.
The horizontal view of the heart
The horizontal view comes from the precordial leads; the hexaxial system determines the axis.
The normal axis of the heart
Correct. Six views in one plane are what make an axis calculable at all.
The duration of the QT interval
Interval durations are measured on the tracing rather than derived from the reference system.

set1.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set1.q: A PR interval measures seven small boxes. How should that be read?
opts: Normal
Seven small boxes exceeds the upper limit of three to five, so the interval is prolonged.
Shortened
Seven small boxes is longer than normal rather than shorter.
Uninterpretable without the heart rate
The PR interval is read against a fixed normal range rather than corrected for rate.
Prolonged, since the normal range is three to five small boxes
Correct. The normal interval runs 0.12 to 0.2 seconds, so seven small boxes is beyond it.

set2.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set2.q: Why are the augmented leads considered unipolar?
opts: They measure between two physical electrodes
Using two physical electrodes is what makes a lead bipolar, which the augmented leads are not.
Only one physical electrode is used
Correct. The machine constructs the other half of the comparison, so there is only one real point of view involved. The rest being created by the machine.
They are placed on the chest rather than the limbs
The augmented leads are limb leads; the chest leads are the precordial ones.
They record no voltage difference at all
They record voltage; the question is how many physical electrodes contribute.

set2.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set2.q: Where is the U wave best seen, and what is it thought to represent?
opts: In lead II, representing atrial repolarisation
It is best seen in the anterior precordial leads, and atrial repolarisation is not the proposed explanation.
In V2 and V3, possibly repolarisation of the Purkinje fibres
Correct, and the hedging is honest: there is no clear understanding of what it represents, so the association with electrolytes is more useful than the theory.
In aVR, representing septal depolarisation
Septal depolarisation is the Q wave, and the U wave is best seen in V2 and V3.
In V5 and V6, representing delayed ventricular filling
The leads are V2 and V3, and the proposal concerns Purkinje repolarisation.

set2.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set2.q: Why is lead II used for rhythm interpretation?
opts: It has a near-perfect view along the heart's vector
Correct. The conduction pathway runs left and down, and lead II looks along that line, so the complexes are at their clearest.
It is the only lead that records atrial activity
Atrial activity appears in other leads too; lead II simply shows it best.
It is unaffected by patient movement
Movement artefact is not the reason; lead II is chosen because it looks along the heart's vector.
It is the only bipolar lead
Leads I and III are bipolar as well; lead II is chosen for its view along the cardiac vector.

set2.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set2.q: Where does the sinoatrial node sit?
opts: At the junction of the atria and the ventricles
That is where the atrioventricular node sits, near the coronary sinus, rather than the sinoatrial node.
Within the interventricular septum
The septum carries the bundle of His and its branches rather than the sinoatrial node.
In the upper wall of the right atrium
Correct, and being the highest pacemaker in the chain is what makes it the one that normally sets the rate. Just below the opening of the vena cava.
In the wall of the left atrium
It sits in the upper wall of the RIGHT atrium, just below the opening of the vena cava.

set2.io: Identify the standard limb and precordial leads and their proper anatomical placement
set2.q: What are contiguous leads?
opts: Leads placed physically next to one another on the skin
The grouping is by the region of heart viewed rather than by skin position.
Leads that share a single physical electrode
Sharing an electrode is not what defines a contiguous group.
Two or more leads looking at the same area of the heart
Correct, which is why a change appearing in a contiguous group means more than the same change in one isolated lead.
Leads recorded at the same moment in time
All leads are recorded together; contiguity refers to the area viewed.

set2.io: Define depolarization and repolarization
set2.q: What does depolarisation represent, and what is its relationship to contraction?
opts: Recovery of cardiac tissue, and it follows contraction
Recovery is repolarisation; depolarisation is activation and it comes before contraction.
Activation of cardiac tissue, occurring simultaneously with contraction
The activation precedes the contraction rather than coinciding with it.
The resting state of the cell between beats
The resting state is phase four, which is neither depolarisation nor repolarisation.
Activation of cardiac tissue, and it precedes contraction
Correct, and the order matters: the electrical event comes first, so an electrocardiogram showing depolarisation does not prove the muscle actually contracted.

set2.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set2.q: Which property refers to a cardiac cell's ability to produce its own impulse?
opts: Automaticity
Correct. It is why the heart beats without instruction from anywhere else, and why several parts of it can take over pacemaking if the one above fails.
Excitability
Excitability is the ability to respond to an impulse or stimulus rather than to generate one.
Conductivity
Conductivity is the ability to pass an impulse from one myocyte to the next.
Contractility
Contractility is the ability of the cell to shorten, which is the mechanical consequence rather than the electrical origin.

set2.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set2.q: What does a BIPOLAR lead measure?
opts: The voltage difference between two distinct body points
Correct. Two real electrodes with a defined polarity, which is what separates leads I, II and III from the rest. One positive and one negative.
The electrical activity from one electrode reference point
That describes a unipolar lead, which is what the augmented and precordial leads are.
The average of all ten electrodes simultaneously
No lead is described as averaging all ten; the bipolar leads compare two points.
The mechanical movement of the chamber beneath it
Electrocardiography measures electrical activity rather than mechanical movement.

set2.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set2.q: Why is the TP segment the best place to assess the isoelectric line?
opts: It is the longest segment on the tracing
Length is not the reason; the absence of electrical activity is.
It represents the resting state of the cardiac cells, between one T wave and the next P wave
Correct. Nothing electrical is happening there, so it gives the truest baseline against which to judge elevation or depression elsewhere.
It contains the J point
The J point sits between the QRS complex and the ST segment.
It is unaffected by lead placement
All parts of the tracing depend on lead placement; the TP segment is chosen because the cells are at rest.

set2.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set2.q: Which of these can an electrocardiogram NOT tell you?
opts: Whether there is electrical activity in the heart
That is precisely what it does show, along with rate, rhythm and the origin of the impulse.
Where the impulse originates
The origin of the impulse is one of the things it can show, along with rate and conduction problems.
Whether there are conduction problems
Conduction problems are among the things it identifies; what it cannot give is haemodynamic status.
Whether the patient has a pulse
Correct, along with haemodynamic status and cardiac output. It shows electrical activity, and electrical activity without a pulse is a recognised and lethal state.

set2.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set2.q: Into how many fascicles does the left bundle branch divide, and what are they?
opts: Two: the left anterior and the left posterior
A third, the interventricular septal fascicle, is described alongside these two.
Four, one to each wall of the ventricle
Three fascicles are described: the left posterior, the interventricular septal and the left anterior.
Three: left anterior, left posterior and septal
Correct. The septal fascicle is the one most often forgotten, which matters because the three-fascicle arrangement is what makes bifascicular block possible. The left anterior.
It does not divide; it terminates directly in Purkinje fibres
It divides into fascicles before becoming the Purkinje network.

set2.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set2.q: Which property allows an impulse to spread from one myocyte to the next?
opts: Conductivity
Correct. It is what turns a single cell's discharge into a coordinated wave across the whole muscle.
Automaticity
Automaticity is the ability to generate an impulse rather than to pass one along.
Excitability
Excitability is the ability to respond to a stimulus, which is a property of the receiving cell rather than of the spread itself.
Contractility
Contractility is the mechanical response to the impulse rather than its propagation.

set2.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set2.q: What does a lead record when the overall vector is net zero?
opts: A negative deflection
A negative deflection means the vector points away rather than cancelling.
A positive deflection
A positive deflection means the vector points toward the lead.
Electrical noise
A net zero vector gives a genuine isoelectric trace rather than artefact.
An isoelectric line
Correct. A flat trace is a finding rather than an absence of one: it says the forces cancelled in that lead's direction. With no deflection.

set2.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set2.q: What is the ionic arrangement during phase 4, the resting state?
opts: More potassium inside the cell
Correct. That separation is the stored charge the cell spends when it fires, and restoring it is what the later phases achieve. With sodium and calcium outside.
More sodium inside the cell, with potassium outside
The arrangement is the other way round: potassium is the ion held inside at rest.
Equal concentrations of all ions across the membrane
An equal distribution would leave no voltage across the membrane, and the resting cell holds a substantial one.
Calcium inside the cell with potassium outside
Calcium sits outside at rest and enters later, during the plateau.

set2.io: Identify the standard limb and precordial leads and their proper anatomical placement
set2.q: A standard twelve-lead electrocardiogram uses how many physical electrodes?
opts: Ten
Correct. Each electrode is a different point of view, and the machine derives twelve views from the ten it is given.
Twelve
Twelve is the number of derived views rather than the number of electrodes placed.
Six
Six is the number of precordial leads rather than the total electrode count.
Fifteen
Ten electrodes are placed for a standard twelve-lead tracing.

set2.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set2.q: In what order do the five phases of the cardiac action potential occur?
opts: Phase 0, then 1, 2, 3 and 4
This reads the numbers in order, but the cycle begins at the resting state, which is phase four.
Phase 4, then 0, 1, 2 and 3
Correct. The numbering does not run in order, which is exactly why it is worth learning as a sequence rather than as a list: rest is phase four, and the upstroke that follows it is phase zero.
Phase 1, then 2, 3, 4 and 0
Neither the starting point nor the order matches the described sequence.
Phase 4, then 3, 2, 1 and 0
The sequence runs from phase four into phase zero and then upward, not downward.

set2.io: Define depolarization and repolarization
set2.q: What happens to the membrane during depolarisation?
opts: It becomes more negative
Becoming more negative is the direction of repolarisation, returning toward rest.
It becomes less negative
Correct. The cell moves away from its resting negativity, which is what the word depolarisation describes.
It holds steady at its resting voltage
Holding steady describes the resting state rather than depolarisation.
It loses all charge separation entirely
The membrane becomes less negative rather than losing charge separation completely.

set2.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set2.q: Which internodal tract does the majority of the population use?
opts: The middle tract
The middle tract is one of the three but is not the one most people use.
The inferior posterior, or slow, tract
The slow tract is one of the three but is not the predominant route.
All three equally
The superior anterior tract predominates rather than the three sharing the load.
The superior anterior, or fast, tract
Correct. The other two usually terminate before reaching the atrioventricular node, so the fast tract does most of the work.

set2.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set2.q: How much time does one small box on electrocardiogram paper represent?
opts: 0.2 seconds
That is the value of one LARGE box, made up of five small ones.
0.1 seconds
Neither box carries this value: a small box is 0.04 seconds and a large one 0.2 seconds.
0.04 seconds
Correct, and five of them make a large box at 0.2 seconds, so five large boxes cover one second.
1 second
One second is covered by five large boxes rather than by one small one.

set2.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set2.q: What must a deflection do to count as a true S wave?
opts: Extend below the baseline
Correct. If it does not, it is called an S wave pattern instead, which is a distinction of naming that matters when describing a tracing precisely.
Follow the T wave
The S wave follows the R wave, well before the T wave; what defines it is crossing the baseline.
Exceed one small box in amplitude
The defining requirement is crossing the baseline rather than reaching an amplitude.
Appear in every lead
Not all three QRS waves are present in every lead or every rhythm.

set2.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set2.q: Which leads are bipolar?
opts: aVR, aVL and aVF
These are augmented leads, and because each uses only one physical electrode they are unipolar.
V1 through V6
The precordial leads measure between the lead and the heart, which makes them unipolar.
Leads I, II and III
Correct. They form the imaginary triangle across the shoulders and the left lower body, and everything else on a twelve-lead tracing is unipolar.
All twelve leads
Only leads I, II and III are bipolar; the augmented and precordial leads are unipolar.

set2.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set2.q: What is noted about the length of the right bundle branch?
opts: It is much shorter than the left, in proportion to the smaller right ventricle
It is described as the longer of the two despite serving the smaller chamber.
It is much longer than the left, despite the left ventricle being the larger chamber
Correct, and the counterintuitiveness is the point: the anatomy does not follow chamber size.
The two are of equal length
They are explicitly contrasted: the right bundle branch is much longer despite serving the smaller ventricle.
It does not reach the Purkinje network
It terminates in the Purkinje network, as the left bundle branch does through its fascicles.

set2.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set2.q: What does the peak of the T wave mark?
opts: The end of ventricular depolarisation
Ventricular depolarisation ends with the QRS complex rather than at the peak of the T wave.
The start of atrial repolarisation
Atrial repolarisation is not represented as a distinct feature here.
The beginning of the ST segment
The ST segment begins at the J point and ends at the onset of the T wave.
The dividing line between the absolute and the relative refractory period
Correct, which is what makes a stimulus landing near the T wave peak so consequential: the cell has just become excitable again.

set2.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set2.q: A corrected QT of 520 milliseconds is reported. How should that be read?
opts: Normal
Normal values top out in the mid four hundreds, so this is well beyond them.
Borderline prolongation
The borderline band runs up to five hundred; this exceeds it.
Shortened
This value is prolonged rather than short, and beyond five hundred milliseconds it is high risk.
High risk prolongation
Correct. Beyond five hundred milliseconds is the high risk band, above the borderline range that begins in the low four hundreds.

set2.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set2.q: What is the J point?
opts: The peak of the T wave
The peak of the T wave divides the absolute from the relative refractory period.
The start of the P wave
The P wave marks the start of atrial depolarisation rather than this junction.
The junction where the QRS complex ends and the ST segment begins
Correct, and it should sit at the baseline, with about a millimetre of variance tolerated.
The end of the T wave
The end of the T wave closes the QT interval rather than marking the J point.

set2.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set2.q: What does the PR interval include?
opts: Atrial depolarisation, the delay at the atrioventricular node, and conduction through the His-Purkinje system
Correct. Three events in one measurement, which is why a prolonged PR interval does not by itself say where the hold-up is.
Ventricular depolarisation and repolarisation
Those are covered by the QRS complex and the T wave respectively.
Atrial depolarisation only
Atrial depolarisation alone is the P wave; the interval extends to the start of the QRS.
The resting state of the cardiac cells
The resting state is represented by the TP segment rather than by any wave.

set2.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set2.q: What does the QT interval span?
opts: From the start of the P wave to the start of the QRS complex
That is the PR interval, which covers atrial depolarisation and the nodal delay.
From the start of the QRS complex to the end of the T wave
Correct, which makes it all of the ventricular activity in one cardiac cycle, depolarisation and repolarisation together.
From the end of the T wave to the next P wave
That is the TP segment, representing the resting state and giving the best isoelectric baseline.
Between two consecutive R waves
That is the R to R interval, used for rate, regularity and the assessment of heart blocks.

set2.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
set2.q: What characterises phase 1, early repolarisation?
opts: Calcium channels open, producing contraction
Calcium entry and contraction belong to phase two, the plateau, rather than to early repolarisation.
Sodium channels close and potassium channels reopen
Correct. The inward current stops and an outward one resumes, which begins bringing the membrane back down.
Fast sodium channels open
Sodium channel opening is phase zero; in phase one they close.
The membrane returns fully to minus ninety millivolts
The full return to resting voltage is completed in phase three rather than phase one.

set2.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
set2.q: What does a cardiac vector represent?
opts: The direction of blood flow through the chambers
It describes electrical activity rather than mechanical flow.
The strength of contraction alone
It carries direction as well as magnitude, and it is electrical rather than mechanical.
The direction and strength of the electrical impulse
Correct. Both quantities at once, which is why it is drawn as an arrow rather than described as a line.
The position of the heart within the chest
It describes the electrical impulse rather than anatomical position.

set2.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
set2.q: Why is the corrected QT used rather than the raw QT interval?
opts: The raw QT cannot be measured accurately on standard paper
It can be measured; the issue is that its value depends on rate.
The corrected value uses different units
Both are expressed in milliseconds, and the normal values are the same figures.
The raw QT applies only to men
Both raw and corrected values have separate figures for men and women.
The QT interval changes with heart rate
Correct. Without correcting, the same heart would appear to have a different QT at different rates. The correction accounts for it.
